setup: A first-time entrepreneur opens the GAMMA-J Web Store from a browser and is preparing to start an online shop with no prior e-commerce experience.
action: The entrepreneur begins exploring the system to set up and run a basic retail storefront.
expected_observation: The platform presents a simple, store-owner-oriented web store experience suitable for creating and operating an online retail business without requiring advanced technical knowledge.

setup: A small business owner with limited technical skills signs in to GAMMA-J Web Store for the first time.
action: The owner starts the onboarding or store setup process.
expected_observation: The system supports a quick start workflow that helps the seller get online without requiring configuration tasks beyond basic business information.

setup: A store owner is signed in with store-owner privileges and the management dashboard is available.
action: The store owner opens the product management and customer account sections.
expected_observation: The owner can view, add, edit, and review product listings and customer accounts from the administration interface.

setup: A sales staff member is signed in with staff-level access to the store backend.
action: The staff member opens the product and customer record management areas.
expected_observation: The staff member can handle product records and customer records within the permissions assigned to sales staff.

setup: A customer is signed in to the web store storefront or is browsing as a customer with shopping access.
action: The customer navigates through product listings, adds an item to the cart, and proceeds to checkout.
expected_observation: The customer can browse products, maintain items in a shopping cart, and place an order through the online store.

setup: The web store contains at least one published product and the customer is on the storefront home page.
action: The customer opens the product catalog or searches the storefront for available items.
expected_observation: The system displays available products with enough information for the customer to browse the catalog, such as names, prices, and product details.

setup: A customer is browsing products and has an active shopping cart on the store site.
action: The customer adds an item to the cart, changes the quantity of an existing item, and removes another item from the cart.
expected_observation: The cart updates accordingly, showing the current items and totals after each change, and retains the customer's selections during the shopping session.

setup: A customer has selected one or more products, entered shipping details, and the cart is ready for checkout.
action: The customer submits the order online.
expected_observation: The system accepts the order, creates a confirmed purchase record, and presents an order confirmation with an order number or equivalent confirmation detail.

setup: A store owner is logged in to the management console with permission to edit the product catalog.
action: The owner adds a new product or updates an existing product's name, description, price, or inventory information.
expected_observation: The product is saved successfully and the catalog reflects the new or updated product information.

setup: A store owner is signed in and customer account records exist in the system.
action: The owner opens a customer account record from the administration area.
expected_observation: The system displays the selected customer account details for review, including the stored account information available to the owner.

setup: New customer orders have been submitted through the storefront and are awaiting staff or owner review.
action: The store owner opens the incoming orders queue or order management screen.
expected_observation: The system lists the incoming orders with their current status and order details so the owner can review them.

setup: A sales staff member is signed in and a product has a current stock or availability status.
action: The staff member changes the product availability, such as marking the item in stock, out of stock, or limited availability.
expected_observation: The updated availability status is saved and is reflected in the store's product record and storefront display.

setup: A sales staff member is signed in and an existing order record contains incorrect customer or product information.
action: The staff member edits the order details to correct the error and saves the changes.
expected_observation: The order record is updated with the corrected information and the revised order data is visible in the order management view.

setup: A new seller starts account onboarding in the web store for the first time.
action: The seller opens the guided setup assistant or onboarding wizard.
expected_observation: The system launches a guided setup flow that leads the seller through the initial configuration steps instead of requiring manual setup of the store from scratch.

setup: A new seller has just entered the guided setup flow and has not yet provided any store profile data.
action: The seller proceeds to the first setup step.
expected_observation: The setup flow begins with a form or screen requesting basic store information such as store name and similar foundational details.

setup: The store owner is in the initial setup flow for a new GAMMA-J Web Store account and has not yet created any categories, products, or customer account settings.
action: The owner opens the setup wizard and enters at least one product category, one sample product, and basic customer account settings such as account visibility and registration preferences.
expected_observation: The setup wizard provides fields for categories, products, and customer account settings, accepts the entries, and confirms that the store setup can proceed with those sections completed.

setup: The store owner is on a setup page that is requesting product and account information for the first time.
action: The owner views the setup form before entering data.
expected_observation: Each section shows clear example values and short prompts in plain language, such as sample category names and sample product details, so the owner understands what to enter.

setup: The store owner is filling out the initial setup form for categories, products, and account settings.
action: The owner leaves a required field blank, such as the product name or category name, and moves to the next step.
expected_observation: The blank required field is flagged immediately on the form, with a visible inline warning before the owner completes setup.

setup: The store owner is completing initial setup and has entered invalid or incomplete information in a required setup field.
action: The owner submits the setup step with a missing category name or an invalid account setting.
expected_observation: The system displays a plain-language explanation of the mistake, identifies what needs to be corrected, and keeps the owner in setup until the error is fixed.

setup: A store administrator has an existing product catalog and order history in the web store.
action: The administrator edits an existing product price and changes the status of an order from pending to shipped.
expected_observation: A change log entry is created for each edit, showing what changed, when it changed, and which record was updated.

setup: The store has active inventory, customer accounts, and orders, and notifications are enabled for staff users.
action: A product stock level drops, an order is cancelled, and a customer account detail is updated.
expected_observation: Staff receive notifications for the stock change, the cancelled order, and the customer account edit, with each notification clearly identifying the type of update.

setup: A staff user is viewing the change log and notification center for the first time.
action: The staff user opens the help or guidance area associated with logs and notifications.
expected_observation: The system shows brief tips and plain-language summaries explaining what the log entries and notifications mean, without using technical jargon.

setup: A new staff user has just signed in after account activation and has not yet reviewed the dashboard.
action: The user starts the onboarding walkthrough.
expected_observation: A short guided tour highlights where to find recent changes and explains the meaning of common notifications in simple language before ending.

setup: The initial release is configured with at least one enabled mainstream payment gateway, and the store is ready to process payments.
action: A customer completes checkout using the supported payment gateway.
expected_observation: The order is submitted through the gateway, the payment attempt is processed, and the customer receives a clear payment result on screen.

setup: The initial release is configured with at least one supported shipping carrier integration, and an order is ready for fulfillment.
action: A staff member requests shipping rates or creates a shipment for an eligible order.
expected_observation: The system retrieves carrier shipping options or shipment data through the integrated carrier and displays the available shipping information to the staff member.

setup: A customer has attempted to pay for an order and the payment gateway has returned a failure response.
action: A staff user opens the order details after the failed payment attempt.
expected_observation: The order is clearly marked as unpaid, and the payment failure status is visible to staff in the order view.

setup: A customer is on the checkout or payment retry page after an initial payment failure.
action: The customer selects retry payment or chooses a different payment method and submits the payment again.
expected_observation: The system allows the customer to resubmit payment, shows the alternative payment method options or retry action, and updates the payment status based on the new attempt.

setup: A store staff user is subscribed to operational alerts for shipping events.
action: A carrier update is delayed beyond the expected time or the shipping update request fails.
expected_observation: The system alerts staff that the shipping update is delayed or failed, and the alert identifies the affected shipment or order.

setup: A payment or shipping issue has occurred for an order that requires staff intervention.
action: A staff user opens the affected order and selects a manual retry or override option.
expected_observation: The system provides a manual retry or override action for the issue and records that the staff member used it instead of blocking the action entirely.

setup: A staff member is authorized to perform a manual override or retry on a payment or shipping issue.
action: The staff member applies the override or retry and enters a reason for the action.
expected_observation: The system stores an audit entry showing who performed the action, the time it occurred, the affected order or shipment, and the reason provided.

setup: An order in the GAMMA-J Web Store has already been flagged with a payment authorization failure or a shipping address error while the customer service agent is signed in.
action: The agent opens the affected order details and triggers the issue notification view.
expected_observation: An in-app alert banner or toast is shown on screen identifying the payment or shipping error, with the affected order reference and a clear message describing the problem.

setup: A high-severity order issue has been unresolved beyond the configured escalation period, and the operations email account is enabled for notifications.
action: The issue remains unresolved until the escalation threshold is reached.
expected_observation: An email notification is sent to the configured recipients stating that a serious or long-unresolved issue requires attention, including the issue type and order reference.

setup: The support dashboard is open and there is at least one unresolved order issue in the system.
action: The dashboard refreshes or the support agent navigates to the issue overview area.
expected_observation: A visible dashboard indicator appears showing unresolved issue count or status, allowing the agent to see that open issues still require attention.

setup: An order contains both a failed payment attempt and a shipping address validation problem.
action: The support agent opens the issue list or order exception queue for that order.
expected_observation: The payment failure is displayed ahead of the shipping issue in the issue order, queue, or alert summary, indicating higher priority for payment problems.

setup: A shopper is on the checkout page with order details entered but has not yet submitted the order.
action: The shopper clicks the Submit Order button.
expected_observation: The system performs pre-submission validation and prevents submission if basic order data is incomplete or malformed, showing validation feedback before the order is accepted.

setup: A customer is on checkout with a missing shipping street address and a credit card number entered in an invalid format.
action: The customer attempts to submit the order.
expected_observation: The checkout page highlights the missing required address field and the obvious payment format issue, with clear messages indicating what must be corrected before submission.

setup: A checkout form is partially completed with customer name missing, shipping details incomplete, and payment information absent or invalid.
action: The shopper submits the order from the checkout screen.
expected_observation: The system blocks order submission and displays validation messages for required customer, shipping, and payment information that must be provided before the order can proceed.

setup: A user is completing the checkout form and has entered values that fail validation, such as an invalid postal code or malformed card number.
action: The user finishes the form or attempts to submit the order.
expected_observation: Validation feedback is shown immediately on the checkout screen or before submission is accepted, making the problem visible without leaving the form.

setup: The checkout page is displaying validation errors for a missing required field or invalid payment detail.
action: The customer edits the invalid field to correct the error.
expected_observation: The customer remains on the same checkout page, the form is preserved, and the customer can continue correcting fields without losing entered information or navigating away.

setup: An administrator is on the product import screen and has access to a spreadsheet file containing product data.
action: The administrator uploads a spreadsheet product file for import.
expected_observation: The system accepts the spreadsheet format for product import and moves the file into the import workflow for review or validation.

setup: An administrator is on the product import screen and has a CSV file containing product records.
action: The administrator uploads the CSV file for product import.
expected_observation: The system accepts the CSV format and begins the product import workflow rather than rejecting the file solely because it is CSV.

setup: An administrator is preparing to import product data from a file that contains field names and sample records.
action: The administrator uploads the file, maps source columns to product fields, and requests a preview before committing the import.
expected_observation: The system presents field mapping options, a preview of the mapped records, and validation results before any product data is permanently imported.

setup: A product import review screen shows one or more record errors, such as a missing SKU or invalid price value.
action: The administrator corrects the problem fields in the review screen and revalidates the import.
expected_observation: The import issues can be corrected without restarting the import process, and the corrected records proceed through validation again from the same session.

setup: A product import has completed with a mix of valid rows, skipped rows, and rows that still need attention.
action: The import finishes and the results page is displayed.
expected_observation: A clear import summary is shown identifying which products were imported successfully, which rows were skipped, and which records require attention or correction.

setup: The import review screen is open and one or more product rows contain fixable errors in editable fields.
action: The user edits the incorrect values directly within the review table before confirming import.
expected_observation: The problem fields are editable inline on the review screen, allowing the user to correct them in place and continue the import without leaving the page.

setup: The import wizard is open with a product CSV loaded, and the file contains at least one row that matches an existing store product by SKU and product name.
action: The merchant proceeds to the duplicate-check step of the import wizard and reviews the matching record.
expected_observation: The wizard identifies the duplicate record and presents the choices to keep the imported row, merge it with the existing product, or skip it.

setup: The merchant has mapped columns for a product import, and at least one row is missing required data or contains inconsistent values such as a blank product title or mismatched unit.
action: The merchant advances from column mapping to the final review step before starting the import.
expected_observation: A review screen appears listing the problematic rows and fields, with prompts that allow the merchant to resolve missing or inconsistent data before import can be finalized.

setup: The merchant starts the product import wizard from the GAMMA-J Web Store admin area.
action: The merchant navigates through the import workflow from file selection to mapping and review.
expected_observation: The wizard advances through small, clearly separated steps and shows a visible progress indicator that updates to reflect the current step in the import process.

setup: The merchant has uploaded a product file and completed column mapping for fields such as name, price, and category.
action: The merchant confirms the column mapping and continues to the next wizard screen.
expected_observation: The wizard displays a live preview of how the imported product rows will appear after mapping, using the selected source columns and showing sample transformed records.

setup: The import file contains rows with issues such as an invalid price format, an unknown category, and a missing image URL.
action: The merchant opens the validation or review step of the import wizard.
expected_observation: The wizard highlights the affected rows or fields and explains each issue in plain language, such as stating that a price is not a valid number or that a category is not recognized.

setup: The import review screen shows at least one issue with a suggested correction, such as normalizing a unit or replacing a misspelled brand name.
action: The merchant selects one of the issue rows and chooses to fix it, ignore it, or apply the suggested correction.
expected_observation: The wizard provides clear actions for the issue and updates the row accordingly when the merchant applies a fix, ignores the warning, or accepts the suggested correction.

setup: The import wizard has evaluated a batch of product rows and classified some as valid while others still have unresolved issues.
action: The merchant views the summary area of the import review screen.
expected_observation: The wizard displays a clear count of how many items are ready to import and how many items still need attention.

setup: The merchant is on a later step of the import wizard after already completing file selection and column mapping.
action: The merchant clicks the Back button to return to the previous step.
expected_observation: The wizard returns to the prior step and preserves the previously entered import settings so the merchant can correct something that looked wrong.

setup: The merchant imports a product catalog containing product names and descriptions that could support optional enrichment, including category, unit of measure, brand, and cleaner titles.
action: The merchant reaches the suggestion stage of the import wizard.
expected_observation: The wizard presents optional suggestions for category, unit of measure, brand, and improved product titles where applicable.

setup: The import wizard shows one or more suggestions for a product record, such as a suggested category, normalized unit, or cleaner title.
action: The merchant chooses to accept one suggestion, edit another suggestion, and reject a third suggestion.
expected_observation: The wizard applies the accepted suggestion, allows the edited suggestion to be adjusted before use, and leaves the rejected suggestion unchanged.

setup: The imported product file contains a product name and description that strongly indicate a likely category, such as a shirt, laptop accessory, or kitchen utensil.
action: The merchant opens the suggestion panel for that product row.
expected_observation: The system suggests a likely category derived from the product name or description only when the inference is confident enough to present a useful recommendation.

setup: The import contains product rows that do not include a short description or image, and the storefront would benefit from those details for product presentation.
action: The merchant reviews the import recommendations for the affected products.
expected_observation: The wizard prompts for the missing product details and clearly indicates that a short description or image is recommended to improve the storefront presentation.

setup: The imported product data includes common unit terms and spellings such as 'kg', 'kilogram', 'litre', or a misspelled but recognizable unit name.
action: The merchant reaches the optional import helper stage for the affected rows.
expected_observation: The system proposes detected units and spelling-normalized values as optional helpers for review rather than changing the imported data automatically.

setup: The import wizard has identified suggestion candidates for product data, such as a cleaner title or normalized unit.
action: The merchant proceeds through the suggestion screen without explicitly accepting any proposed change.
expected_observation: No silent data changes are applied; each suggestion remains visible for review and requires the merchant's explicit action before it affects the imported data.

setup: The merchant is using the import wizard to load multiple product records with a mix of valid rows and rows requiring review.
action: The merchant advances through the import process and opens the summary or review section.
expected_observation: The wizard shows clear step indicators, plain-language status messages, and a simple count of items ready versus items needing review.

setup: An admin is signed in to GAMMA-J Web Store and is viewing either a product import screen or an existing product record in the catalog manager.
action: The admin imports a product file that includes category values and then edits a product to assign or change its category from the product management screen.
expected_observation: The imported products are placed into the specified categories, and the manually edited product shows the updated category in the catalog without altering other product details.

setup: An admin is creating or editing a product in the catalog, and the product has selectable variations such as size or color.
action: The admin defines variation options for the product and saves it while leaving the product's category assignment unchanged.
expected_observation: The product is saved with its variations displayed separately from its category, and the category remains available as a distinct classification field.

setup: A customer or staff user opens the GAMMA-J Web Store on a desktop or laptop device with a standard web browser.
action: The user navigates through the store pages using only the browser interface.
expected_observation: The store loads and operates in the browser with visible pages, navigation controls, and forms, without requiring a desktop application or separate client.

setup: A user has access to a standard, up-to-date web browser on a device that does not have any GAMMA-J-specific software installed.
action: The user enters the store URL and attempts to browse products and begin checkout.
expected_observation: The web store opens and functions normally in the browser, and the user can browse and start checkout without installing additional software.

setup: A new store owner with limited technical experience is starting initial setup through the web interface.
action: The owner follows the on-screen setup prompts to enter store name, contact details, and basic configuration options.
expected_observation: The interface presents simple step-by-step guidance with clear labels and prompts, helping the owner complete setup without needing technical knowledge or advanced configuration screens.

setup: A customer has placed an order, and the order status later changes to confirmed, cancelled, or refunded by an authorized staff action or system event.
action: The status change is saved for the order.
expected_observation: The system automatically generates and sends the appropriate customer notice, such as an order confirmation, cancellation notice, or refund notification, and the notice reflects the correct order details and status.

setup: A shopper is viewing a product page, cart summary, checkout page, or receipt within GAMMA-J Web Store.
action: The shopper reviews the displayed pricing information before placing the order.
expected_observation: The interface clearly shows the item price and other applicable pricing details, such as totals and any taxes or fees that apply, so the shopper can understand the final cost before completing the purchase.

setup: A new customer is signing up for an account or checking out as part of an order process.
action: The customer enters account and order details in the available forms.
expected_observation: The system requests only the information needed to complete the order or create the customer account, and it does not require unrelated personal data fields.

setup: A customer is on the signup page or checkout page where personal data is collected.
action: The customer views the consent and privacy sections before continuing.
expected_observation: The page displays clear privacy and consent notices, including how customer data will be used, and the customer is required to acknowledge them before proceeding.

setup: An authorized staff member is editing a customer record, adjusting a product price, modifying an order, or recording a payment.
action: The staff member saves the change.
expected_observation: The system records the edit in an audit log with the relevant record type, action, user identity, and timestamp so the change can be reviewed later.

setup: A product exists in the catalog with current stock information, and an authorized staff member has access to inventory controls.
action: The staff member marks the item as out of stock after a sale, updates quantity after a restock, or urgently flags the item as unavailable.
expected_observation: The product availability status updates accordingly in the store and admin views, and an urgent unavailable mark prevents the item from being offered for purchase.

setup: The store is operating under normal customer traffic with multiple users browsing products, updating carts, and placing orders.
action: Several users simultaneously navigate catalog pages, add and remove items from carts, and submit orders during a period of increased seasonal demand.
expected_observation: Browsing, cart changes, and order entry remain responsive, and users receive timely page updates and checkout responses without obvious delays that prevent completion.

setup: The store is under higher-than-normal activity with customers browsing pages, staff processing orders, and staff updating products at the same time.
action: Users continue loading pages, checking out, processing orders, and saving product updates during the active period.
expected_observation: Page loads and core transactional actions remain responsive enough for normal use, and browsing, checkout, staff processing, and product update operations complete without the interface becoming unusable.

setup: The platform is hosting at least two separate stores, each with its own catalog, orders, and customer data.
action: An administrator adds a new store and then changes products, pricing, or settings within that store.
expected_observation: The new store is created as an isolated tenant, and its catalog or settings changes do not alter data or behavior in the existing stores.

setup: The store is actively handling product updates, cart activity, and incoming orders during a period of increased traffic.
action: Customers submit orders and staff save updates to products or payments while the system is under load.
expected_observation: The system saves the changes reliably, and submitted orders and updates remain persisted and retrievable without being lost, duplicated, or silently discarded.

setup: The store is operating in GAMMA-J without a full external inventory system integration, and staff members have access to the product stock management screen.
action: A staff member updates the on-hand quantity for an existing product directly in GAMMA-J and saves the change.
expected_observation: The new stock quantity is stored in GAMMA-J, the updated quantity is shown on the product record, and the system does not require a full inventory system integration to complete the update.

setup: A customer profile exists in the store with saved contact details and order history, and no subscription product or recurring billing service is active for that profile.
action: A staff member views the account details for that customer in the admin area.
expected_observation: The account is displayed as a customer profile containing contact and order information, and it is not labeled or treated as a paid subscription.

setup: The catalog contains products grouped into categories, and one product also has selectable variants such as size or color.
action: A merchandiser opens the catalog management view and inspects the category structure and the variant options for the product.
expected_observation: Categories are shown as navigation and organization labels for products, while the product variations remain separate option values on the product and are not treated as categories.

setup: The initial release environment is configured for checkout using one approved payment gateway and one approved shipping carrier integration.
action: An administrator attempts to enable a second payment gateway and a second shipping carrier during initial release configuration.
expected_observation: The system prevents activation of the additional gateway and carrier, and the configuration remains limited to one payment gateway and one shipping carrier integration.

setup: The store is running the initial release and stock is maintained directly inside GAMMA-J rather than through an external inventory platform.
action: A release planner reviews the inventory setup requirements for go-live.
expected_observation: The release checklist does not require a full inventory system integration, and stock management is accepted as being handled inside GAMMA-J.

setup: A customer checkout attempt has failed because the payment authorization was declined, and the issue is being triaged in the support queue.
action: A support agent reviews the open issues alongside other lower-severity store issues.
expected_observation: The payment failure is flagged as the highest-priority issue and is positioned ahead of non-payment problems in the queue.

setup: The support queue contains a missed dispatch, a shipping address error, and a minor shipping delay report.
action: A fulfillment manager opens the shipping issue list and checks the default priority order.
expected_observation: The missed dispatch and bad address issues are ranked ahead of the minor shipping delay, indicating higher priority for the more serious shipping problems.

setup: A staff member is on a manual override screen for changing an order quantity or product stock level.
action: The staff member attempts to save the override without entering their identity and without providing a reason.
expected_observation: The system blocks the save action, prompts for the staff member identity and reason, and records the change only after both fields are supplied.

setup: An order and a product have both been modified previously by staff members.
action: An admin opens the change history or audit view for the order and the product.
expected_observation: The system displays who made each change and the timestamp for when the change occurred.

setup: A product import file contains new rows where some items share the same product name, SKU, or barcode as existing catalog items.
action: A catalog manager uploads the file through the product import interface.
expected_observation: The import process identifies duplicate candidates using product name, SKU, or barcode when available, and marks the matching rows for review or conflict handling.

setup: A product data cleanup session is open and the catalog contains items with missing prices, inconsistent naming, incorrect category assignments, and unclear stock values.
action: A merchandiser runs the cleanup validation on the product set.
expected_observation: The system highlights each product with missing prices, inconsistent product names, wrong categories, and unclear stock quantities so they can be corrected.

setup: A customer is on the checkout page with items in the cart, and some required order fields are left empty or inconsistent.
action: The customer submits the order without completing the customer, shipping, and payment checks.
expected_observation: The order is not submitted, and the system prompts for customer, shipping, and payment information to be checked before checkout can proceed.

setup: The checkout and account creation forms are configured for minimal data collection.
action: A customer enters only the information needed to place the order and create an account.
expected_observation: The form accepts the minimal set of required fields and does not force unrelated personal data collection beyond what is needed for the order and account.

setup: The product administration area includes an import option for loading catalog data from a spreadsheet file.
action: A catalog manager uploads a spreadsheet containing product names, SKUs, prices, and stock quantities.
expected_observation: The system accepts the spreadsheet as a product data import source and loads the product records from the file.

setup: The initial release is being configured with payment processing enabled and the storefront is ready for checkout testing.
action: An administrator connects one mainstream payment gateway to the checkout flow.
expected_observation: The checkout can process payments through the connected mainstream gateway, confirming support for at least one mainstream payment gateway in the initial release.

setup: A merchant is configuring shipping options for a new GAMMA-J Web Store installation, and the carrier integration feature is enabled for the initial release environment.
action: The merchant opens the shipping settings and selects a supported shipping carrier to connect for rate lookup and label creation.
expected_observation: The system allows the carrier to be connected successfully and displays shipping carrier options, status, or returned rates through the web interface.

setup: A customer or store administrator is ready to use GAMMA-J Web Store on a supported desktop or mobile browser.
action: The user enters the store URL in a standard browser and continues browsing the catalog and checkout pages.
expected_observation: The store loads and functions correctly in the browser, with no requirement for a separate desktop application or browser plug-in.

setup: A first-time shopper with limited technical experience opens the web store on a standard browser.
action: The shopper browses products, adds an item to the cart, and proceeds to checkout using the on-screen navigation.
expected_observation: The interface presents a straightforward layout with obvious next actions, readable labels, and minimal clutter so the shopper can complete the task without needing advanced technical knowledge.

setup: A user opens a page that explains shipping, payment, or account setup in the web store.
action: The user reviews the on-screen instructions and help text while preparing to complete the operation.
expected_observation: The page uses plain language, short explanatory text, and brief tips that explain the task without jargon or technical terms.

setup: A new administrator starts the initial setup process for the web store.
action: The administrator follows the setup flow from start to finish.
expected_observation: The setup is presented as a guided sequence of small steps, with each screen focusing on one clear action before moving to the next.

setup: A user opens the import wizard to bring product data into the web store.
action: The user advances through the import wizard screens.
expected_observation: Each wizard screen asks for one decision or input at a time, with no screen presenting a long list of unrelated choices or crowded controls.

setup: An import validation issue occurs while the user is importing catalog data.
action: The import wizard displays feedback about the problem.
expected_observation: The message is calm and reassuring, explains the issue in practical terms, and tells the user what to do next without sounding alarming or blaming.

setup: A user navigates through product pages, cart pages, or the import wizard in the web store.
action: The system presents warnings, guidance, or status feedback during normal operations.
expected_observation: The interface relies mainly on labels, icons, and inline messages, with limited use of strong colors and no excessive popups or alarm-heavy visuals.

setup: The web store is operating under normal traffic, then during a seasonal spike with many shoppers browsing, checking out, and staff updating products.
action: Multiple users browse products, place items in carts, complete checkout, and administrators save catalog updates at the same time.
expected_observation: The site remains responsive enough for browsing, checkout, order processing, and product updates to continue without noticeable blocking or unusable delays for normal business use.

setup: A user has edited a product, cart setting, or order-related record in the web store and is ready to save the change.
action: The user submits the save action and then revisits the item after the save completes.
expected_observation: The change is stored reliably and appears persisted when the record is re-opened, with no silent loss of the saved data.

setup: The store is processing a higher-than-usual volume of orders and product updates.
action: Customers place orders and staff submit product changes during the increased activity period.
expected_observation: All submitted orders and updates are retained and processed; none disappear, vanish from queues, or fail silently because of the increased load.

setup: A user opens the import wizard to upload or map product data.
action: The user begins the import process and moves through the wizard steps.
expected_observation: The wizard shows a visible progress indicator such as a progress bar and displays the current step label, so the user can see how far the import has advanced.

setup: A user returns to the import wizard after moving through earlier steps.
action: The user advances to the next screen and compares the layout across consecutive steps.
expected_observation: The wizard keeps button placement, terminology, and screen structure consistent from step to step, making the flow predictable and easy to follow.

setup: During import, the system suggests automatic mappings or corrections for incoming data.
action: The user reviews a suggestion and chooses to accept, modify, or reject it.
expected_observation: Automation is offered as an option rather than a requirement, and the user can override the suggestion before the import is finalized.

setup: A user is importing a data file with some records requiring review or correction.
action: The user starts the import and proceeds through the review stages.
expected_observation: The process is broken into small manageable steps, shows clear progress feedback, and includes counts of items that still need attention so the user can understand the remaining workload.

setup: A customer has placed an order in the GAMMA-J Web Store and proceeds to submit payment through the checkout flow; the payment processor returns a failure response.
action: The customer completes the payment step and the failed transaction response is received by the store.
expected_observation: A clear payment failure message is shown to the customer, and the order remains marked as unpaid in the staff order view so support staff can see it needs attention.

setup: An order has already been handed off for shipment tracking, and the shipping status update from the carrier is delayed or cannot be retrieved.
action: The system attempts to refresh the shipping status and receives no update or an error from the shipping source.
expected_observation: Staff receive an alert indicating the shipping update problem, and the customer sees a simple status such as 'Shipping update delayed' or 'Tracking temporarily unavailable' rather than a detailed technical error.

setup: A staff member is handling an order or import issue that requires bypassing a blocking system error using a manual override.
action: The staff member applies the manual override and completes the affected workflow.
expected_observation: The system records the staff member identity, the reason for the override, the original error message, the action taken, and the timestamp in the audit history.

setup: A staff member is importing a file containing product, customer, or order data, and one row or field contains invalid information that prevents the import from completing.
action: The staff member runs the import and the validation error is triggered on the affected row or field.
expected_observation: The import screen shows the problem directly beside the affected row or field, includes a short explanation of what is wrong, and provides a suggested fix the staff member can apply.

setup: A customer is on the checkout page with order details entered, but one or more required validation rules are not satisfied, such as a missing address, invalid postal code, or incomplete contact information.
action: The customer submits the checkout form with the invalid or incomplete order data.
expected_observation: The customer remains on the checkout page and sees exact correction guidance for each validation problem, with the specific fields or entries that must be fixed before the order can be submitted.

setup: The initial release is being prepared, but the payment gateway vendor has not yet been chosen by the team.
action: A product stakeholder reviews the checkout requirements for the payment integration in the release scope.
expected_observation: The requirement remains vendor-agnostic, with no customer-facing behavior or acceptance rule tied to a specific payment gateway brand until the vendor decision is made.

setup: The initial release is being prepared, but the shipping carrier vendor has not yet been chosen by the team.
action: A product stakeholder reviews the shipment and tracking requirements for the release scope.
expected_observation: The requirement remains vendor-agnostic, with no acceptance scenario depending on a specific carrier name or carrier-specific tracking behavior until the vendor decision is confirmed.

setup: The team has identified that only initial payment and shipping support are in scope, while additional integrations and technical constraints are still under review.
action: A release planner reviews the integration scope for the first version of the GAMMA-J Web Store.
expected_observation: The system scope is limited to the confirmed payment and shipping capabilities, and no additional integration behavior or technical constraint assumptions are treated as accepted requirements.

setup: The team has not yet confirmed the legal jurisdictions or consumer protection rules that apply to the store's customer-facing policies and messages.
action: A compliance review is performed for the consumer-facing checkout and policy text.
expected_observation: Jurisdiction-specific compliance behavior is left unresolved, and no final acceptance rule is set for legal wording, disclosures, or rule enforcement until the applicable jurisdictions are verified.
